facts.fact: The Bureau des Normes de Madagascar (BNM), the national standards body (Organisme National de Normalisation), was created by decree no. 98-944 of 4 November 1998 and is now governed by decree no. 2014-1570 of 30 September 2014; the document names no information technology or data standard.

systems.owner: Ministry of Commerce (technical oversight), Ministry of Finance (budget oversight)

note: The BNM has a certification department, but the document names no certification against an IT or data standard and no certified organisation, so no certification fact.
Press release on the handover of the Digital Readiness Assessment; it names no standards body, standard or certification.

facts.fact: The UNDP Digital Readiness Assessment states that Madagascar has a national standards body, the Bureau des Normes de Madagascar, a correspondent member of ISO, and that public information shows no specific programme on AI or data-governance standards; the report gives no date for the body's creation, so its published date is used.

note: Certification: the report says most data centres meet only local rules or custom standards, with no ISO 27001 or SSAE 16 certification, and names no certifier; its ISO 27001 mentions are recommendations, so no certification fact. Proposals to mandate the Bureau to adopt data and AI standards and to launch a Digital Trust label are recommendations, not facts.
The document does not say the BNM was set up by law or issued any national standard.
The document states nothing on national standards for information technology or data.
